sections.title: Studies in Planting Design: Plant-Based Material Workshop
sections.description: This seminar explores plant-based materials as a foundation for experimental landscape architecture. Students will work intensively in the shop and in the field, designing and detailing full scale (1:1) prototypes to test fibers, stalks, roots, leaves, bark, and wood as singular and composite construction materials. The course embraces impermanence: no material lasts forever, and that’s not a flaw but an invitation to rebuild, adapt, and fold new lessons into the next version. Alongside this iterative approach, we’ll experiment with contemporary waste streams and invasive plant re-use, turning ecological challenges into raw material for new design. Pre-industrial and pre-petroleum crafts, coupled with Indigenous and vernacular knowledge, will be reimagined through the lens of modern digital fabrication and carbon sequestration, inviting students to bridge old and new ways of making. Every prototype will be considered not just for its human use, but also for the components, habitats, and structures it can share with other species. By semester’s end, students will have produced a series of 1:1 prototypes that explore durability, decay, reuse, and habitat—reframing what it means to design with plants as material.
